blocks.x: IoT, Twin & Robotics applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Manufacturing & Industrial, iot, digital twin & robotics bridges the physical and digital enterprise: industrial sensor network, digital twin platforms, computer vision and edge ai, predictive maintenance, robotics and autonomous systems integration, connected products, and smart infrastructure. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: industrial iot & sensor network, digital twin platform engineering, computer vision & edge ai — delivered on Dataq Twinverse and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Brownfield instrumentation gap
Critical assets run uninstrumented because gut-and-replace is unthinkable; the data that twins and models need does not exist, and downtime for retrofit is unaffordable.
Quality escapes and manual inspection

Defect detection depends on sampling and eyes; escapes reach customers, and scrap/rework costs hide in the P&L. Vision systems stall in pilot because lighting, thresholds and line integration were never engineered.
Planning by spreadsheet under volatility

Planners fight demand volatility, material shortages and changeovers in spreadsheets; scheduling knowledge lives in two veterans' heads. OEE losses from changeover and waiting are structurally accepted.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 7 services from the IoT, Digital Twin & Robotics tower — Industrial IoT & sensor network, Digital Twin Platform Engineering, Computer Vision & Edge AI, Predictive Maintenance & Asset Intelligence as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: IEC 62443 obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Industrial IoT & Sensor Fabric
Sense everything that matters: retrofit-friendly sensor network with governed telemetry.
Digital Twin Platform Engineering
Simulate before you cut steel: plant, fleet and product twins with governed physics and data.
Computer Vision & Edge AI
Cameras into instruments: inspection, safety and counting at the edge, inside policy.
Predictive Maintenance & Asset Intelligence
Fix it before it fails: RUL models wired into planning, spare parts and work orders.
Retrofit sensor fabric
Ex-rated/industrial sensing on live lines with governed telemetry (critical assets instrumented without stoppage)
Digital twin for capacity
Physics+data twin for line reconfiguration and bottleneck decisions (capital validated before spend)
Root-cause investigation time
From weeks to hours with correlated telemetry
Unplanned downtime on critical assets
Down 30-50% within a year of instrumented prediction
Defect escape rate on instrumented stations
Down sharply with vision closed loops

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: IEC 62443 and ESG reporting (CSRD/ISSB). Plant-level energy and emissions data with auditability. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
